goal: Build a portable AI-coding harness whose rules are enforced by scripts and tests rather than by prose, and measure it with a fixed task set.
_format: Structured state survives contact with an agent better than prose: models are measurably less likely to casually rewrite JSON than narrative Markdown. Keep this file small — it is re-read every session, so it is a recurring context tax.

constraints: HARD-WON: `vitest` green does NOT imply the tree compiles. Always run tsc too — that is the whole reason verify.sh exists.
HARD-WIN: node_modules can be absent on a fresh container; 'tests passed' notes from a previous session are unreproducible until you install and re-measure.

DSH: the web app disables tool-bash/tool-fs/agent-instructions at the TOP level; capabilities actually come from the agent preset (preset-standard). Add capability by editing a preset, not by re-enabling top-level rows.
DSH: profile-level plugin/hook changes need a RESTART. `.agents/skills/` and AGENTS.md are read live — no restart. Prefer the live surfaces.
Playwright renames every download to a GUID when acceptDownloads is on — never assert on filename under Playwright.
Playwright's debugger attachment keeps an MV3 service worker alive indefinitely; you cannot observe the 30 s idle termination with it attached.
Headless extension testing requires channel:'chromium'; the default headless shell silently never starts the service worker, and channel:'chrome' silently ignores --load-extension.
webextension-polyfill is ARCHIVED (final commit 2026-07-30); Chrome 148+ ships the native `browser` namespace.
notVerified: Cases 001/003/005 have only been run once each; single-run pass/fail is a weak signal because model output varies. Repeat runs are needed before treating the baseline as stable.
No real-browser (Playwright) test exists; all chrome API behaviour comes from the hand-written mock, whose fidelity gaps are documented but unfixed.

The skills are confirmed discoverable and their text is injected on demand, but their EFFECT on agent behaviour is unmeasured. That is what tests/cases.json is for, and no before/after harness comparison has been run yet.
The eval cases are smoke tests, not a capability benchmark: two of them (001, 005) key on the same 'tests green, types red' fact and are partly redundant.
